images.name: After the Lantern Went Dark
images.description: Greyreed and the barrow to the north at dusk. The ancient lantern on the summit has gone out.
images.background: Greyreed has thirty-odd households, with daily life centered on its mill, tavern, and small chapel. For a hundred years, the lantern kept watch from the barrow north of the village. Three days ago it suddenly went out. Its lampkeeper disappeared soon afterward.
images.storyContext: This is what the player can learn on arrival. The distance between the hill and the village serves the promotional composition; it must not determine travel distances or map rulings.
visualNotes: Warm window light contrasts with the wetlands beneath a cold gray sky.
The lantern shelter on the summit is dark. The tomb doors halfway up the hill stand open.
Reeds and a dark path in the lower left leave space for the homepage title.

images.name: Greyreed and the Barrow
images.description: A sketch map of the area known at the start. Distances between landmarks are not exact travel distances.
images.background: The road north of Greyreed leads to the Lampkeeper's Cottage and Lantern Barrow. In the village, the tavern, the Reeve's House, the mill, and Dawn Chapel are the main places to begin investigating and gathering a party. Marshland surrounds them, reeds broken by stretches of black water.
images.storyContext: This overview shows only known landmarks above ground. The buildings, waterways, and distances are arranged for illustration. It shows no routes inside the tomb, hidden rooms, or secret locations.
images.location: The known surface region around Greyreed
visualNotes: The barrow is at the top, the village below, with a road connecting them.
The waterwheel, chapel, and antler-marked tavern give each landmark a distinct silhouette.
The map has no text, so the app can overlay place names in the chosen language. Display the whole map without cropping.

images.name: The Crooked Antler
images.description: A hearth, hot ale, and a bounty notice. Your first expedition starts here.
images.background: The Crooked Antler serves as both tavern and inn, and is where Greyreed exchanges its news. Mirelle has a long memory and a tight lip. The reeve is offering thirty silver coins for someone to enter the tomb and bring the lampkeeper home.
images.storyContext: The player opens this door on a rainy late-autumn night. The veteran and the sister are both potential companions to approach. The empty scene leaves space at the bar, in the corner, and by the window for different conversations, without deciding anyone's next move.
visualNotes: The hearth and the cold rain outside contrast the safety within with the unknown beyond.
Hot ale on the bar, a wiping cloth, and the notice echo the everyday details of the opening.
The clear central aisle leaves room to use the scene as a dialogue background.

images.name: The Open Bronze Doors
images.description: Halfway up the hill, the bronze double doors stand wide open, pushed outward. The broken seal lies on the cold, wet stone steps.
images.background: The bronze tomb doors halfway up the barrow opened the night the lantern went out. The seal shows that it was pushed open from inside. Ysolde entered with her lamp; no one in the village has seen her since.
images.storyContext: The tomb doors are one of the first definite locations the expedition encounters. Players can examine the seal, prepare their lights, and decide how to enter. The picture reveals nothing about what lies deeper in the tomb.
visualNotes: The double doors open outward, with broken fittings lying before the cold, wet threshold.
Verdigris, moss, and standing water show years of weathering in the marsh climate.
Inside, stone steps descend into darkness. The designs on the doors are decorative, not clues to decipher.

images.name: The Hall of Lamps
images.description: Wall lamps line the stone passage into darkness. A few have been relit, showing the way ahead.
images.background: The Hall of Lamps is the first passage beyond the barrow entrance, with lamps along both walls. The lampkeeper says relighting them sends the barrow deeper into sleep. Noise, fighting, and delays make the expedition more dangerous.
images.storyContext: This scene imagines a moment during exploration after some wall lamps have been relit. It does not mean they are already burning in a new session, or that the lantern on the summit has been restored.
visualNotes: Warm pools of lamplight repeat along the niches on both walls; many lamps are still dark.
The damp flagstones catch a little light, while the far end remains out of sight.
No characters or enemies occupy the center, leaving room for different parties to explore.

images.name: Brannoc Hale
images.description: A fifty-year-old retired soldier who has spent three days brooding over his drink in a corner of the Crooked Antler. He says he's just passing through, but keeps staring toward the barrow. His sword is old but well kept.
images.background: A gruff veteran with a soft heart who steps in front of others first and complains later.
images.storyContext: A portrait for character introductions and dialogue. It does not establish that the player has found this person, and it leaves later actions and outcomes open.

images.name: Sister Wren
images.description: A nineteen-year-old acolyte of the Order of the Dawn Lantern, sent to Greyreed to inspect the barrow lantern. She arrived three days late. She can heal wounds and read the ancient lantern inscriptions, and hides a question about her faith.
images.background: Sincere, conscientious, and braver than she looks. Recites prayers when nervous.
images.storyContext: A portrait for character introductions and dialogue. It does not establish that the player has found this person, and it leaves later actions and outcomes open.

images.name: Mirelle Voss
images.description: Owner of the Crooked Antler, early forties, with a long memory, a tight lip, and exact accounts. Every rumor in the village reaches her bar first.
images.background: Shrewd and warm; she hands you the truth only once she's sure you're worth it.
images.storyContext: A portrait for character introductions and dialogue. It does not establish that the player has found this person, and it leaves later actions and outcomes open.

images.name: Reeve Aldous Penn
images.description: Greyreed's reeve, who posted the bounty in the tavern. He wants the matter settled quickly, but is evasive about the days before the lampkeeper disappeared.
images.background: Respectable and anxious. Habitually hides his own mistakes behind rules and procedure.
images.storyContext: A portrait for character introductions and dialogue. It does not establish that the player has found this person, and it leaves later actions and outcomes open.

images.name: Lampkeeper Ysolde
images.description: In her seventies, Ysolde has tended the barrow lantern for forty years. Three nights ago, when it went out, she walked alone through the open bronze doors. She hasn't come out.
images.background: A stubborn, clear-headed old woman who knows the truth about the barrow. She would rather shoulder the burden herself than frighten the villagers.
images.storyContext: A portrait for character introductions and dialogue. It does not establish that the player has found this person, and it leaves later actions and outcomes open.

images.name: Corvin Ashe
images.description: A young scholar from the capital. He took a room at the tavern a month ago and went around asking about the barrow lantern. He checked out the day before it went out. No one saw him leave the village.
images.background: Clever, charming, and dangerously self-assured. He believes knowledge is its own justification.
images.storyContext: A portrait for character introductions and dialogue. It does not establish that the player has found this person, and it leaves later actions and outcomes open.
